title: Light-years, Parsecs and Astronomical Units
h1: Light-years, parsecs and AU — the three scales of astronomy
description: Astronomers switch units by discipline: AU for planets, parsecs for stars, light-years for the public. Here is how the three scales relate and when each is used.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: The parsec is defined by geometry. The light-year is defined by time. The AU is defined by our own orbit. Three units, three eras, one very big sky.
body: Astronomers rarely use metres. Distances are enormous, and the units that survive in professional literature match the measurement technique. Radar-ranged planets get AU. Parallax-measured stars get parsecs. Everything else gets light-years, mostly for the press release.

> 1 AU = 149,597,870,700 m (exact, IAU 2012)
> 1 light-year = 9.4607 × 10¹⁵ m ≈ 63,241 AU
> 1 parsec = 3.0857 × 10¹⁶ m ≈ 3.2616 ly
> 1 kiloparsec = 3,261.6 ly; 1 megaparsec = 3.26 million ly

A parsec is the distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond of parallax. That definition matches directly to what a telescope measures — an angle over six months as Earth swings around the Sun. Converting parallax to a light-year distance adds a factor of 3.26 that carries no physical meaning, so professionals skip the step.
## The AU and Kepler's third law

In AU-and-years units, Kepler's third law reduces to T² = a³ for objects orbiting the Sun. A planet at 4 AU orbits in 8 years. A comet at 100 AU aphelion takes 500-year loops. The unit choice makes the physics fall out cleanly — one reason the IAU keeps the AU alive alongside SI metres.

Proxima Centauri sits at a parallax of 0.7687 arcsec, giving 1/0.7687 = 1.301 parsecs = 4.244 light-years = 268,553 AU = 4.014 × 10¹⁶ m. Each unit tells a different story: the parsec tells you the measurement was clean, the light-year tells you the signal delay is 4.24 years, the AU compares it to the Solar System (2,700× wider than Neptune's orbit).
AU for planets, parsec for stars, light-year for anything you need a general audience to feel. And 1 pc ≈ 3.26 ly, always.

faqs.q: Is the Kessel Run in 12 parsecs a mistake?
faqs.a: A parsec is a distance, not a time — but Star Wars justified it as a shorter route around a black hole cluster. It still bothers astronomers.

faqs.q: How far is the nearest galaxy in parsecs?
faqs.a: Andromeda is at about 780 kiloparsecs, or 2.54 million light-years.
It was redefined as an exact conventional value in 2012 so that AU-based calculations no longer depend on measuring the Sun's mass.
